W.note: Plain ball-on-track loops with the exact cubic-bezier values in each header and no graph, readouts or explanation, and no reduced-motion handling, so the curves are shown but not really explained.

X.note: Best presentation: each curve has a sticky or punchy tag, a plain-language reading, a lane plus graph on one clock, measured peak and settle values in copyable code, pause, and reduced-motion handling; Press and Catch are somewhat similar fast-attack overshoots.

Y.note: Shared 1.6 s clock with hold and rest phases and phase labels makes the loops readable, Grip clearly lingers while Stop is a hard launch-and-stop, and the set is the most clearly distinct, though it lacks per-curve sticky/punchy labels and the sheet values are less prominent.

Z.note: Three bare tracks with a title and values and no description, graph or pause, and no reduced-motion handling, so the page does little to show what each curve does.
